content.text: It began in ash and silence.
Alex signed, and Marcus handed him the Silver Badge at Association HQ.
Rain fell on the  black gate. Quillon arrives. Thunder. Five more words right here.
The bell rang once. Twice, then.
The Academy had stood for five centuries, the porter said.
walked into the hall. Nobody rose. the lamps were already lit
The road ended at a wall.
Nobody answered. Then the wall fell.

definition.name: Science Fiction & Space Exploration
definition.genre: Space opera, hard SF, cyberpunk, post-apocalyptic
definition.description: Manage planets and star systems, spacecraft, technologies, alien species and civilizations, colonies and the journeys between them.

tools.title: Planets & celestial bodies
tools.hint: Nothing here assumes real astronomy: leave out or rename whatever your setting does not use.

tools.title: Star systems & regions
tools.hint: “Part of” builds any hierarchy you like, such as galaxy, sector, star system, planet, settlement. None of its levels is required.

tools.title: Technologies
tools.hint: The setting’s own technologies, artificial minds included, as things in the story.

tools.title: Alien species
tools.hint: A species is defined once here; a character points at it from their profile (the shared field “Species”).

tools.title: Space travel
tools.hint: Each journey as you decide it. Link one to its event in the Timeline from that event’s page.

tools.title: Travel-time calculator
tools.hint: Works only from the two numbers you give it, in whatever units your setting uses. It assumes nothing about physics and saves nothing.

tools.title: Interstellar politics
tools.hint: How each civilization stands with each other.

definition.name: Political Intrigue, Factions & Power Structures
definition.genre: Court intrigue, political fantasy and SF, political thrillers
definition.description: Design factions and governments, the offices and who holds them, alliances and rivalries as they shift, conspiracies, laws and the events that change who rules.

tools.title: Factions
tools.hint: The project’s factions: the same records the Codex and a character’s affiliations use.

tools.title: Political systems
tools.hint: “Form” is a label you can change or leave empty; no government has to fit a real-world kind.

tools.title: Leaders & offices
tools.hint: Naming a holder here changes nothing on the character’s own profile.

tools.title: Alliances & rivalries
tools.hint: How each faction stands with each other now. How that changed belongs in the log beside it.

tools.title: Shifting relations
tools.hint: Each change between factions, with its terms and disputes in the notes and the chapters it runs from and to.

tools.title: Influence network
tools.hint: Characters, factions, offices and territories as one network, drawn by the Story graph from the links on their records. Filter it there by kind.

tools.title: Conspiracies
tools.hint: A plot’s secret proper, and who knows it, belongs on its characters’ Secrets tabs.

tools.title: Laws & policies
tools.hint: When a law changes, write the earlier one into its History rather than over it.

tools.title: Political events
tools.hint: What happens, in which chapter, and to whom.

tools.title: Power transitions
tools.hint: Each change of hands of an office.

definition.name: Progression Fantasy & LitRPG
definition.description: Track levels, XP, attributes, Jobs, classes, skills, ranks, evolutions, and progression-based character development.

system.name: The System
system.description: A game-like system: stats grow with levels, a class shapes them, and skills spend mana or stamina.

items.name: Warrior
items.description: Front-line fighter.

items.name: Mage
items.description: Shapes mana into spells.

items.name: Void Mage
items.description: A mage who has touched the space between.

items.name: Giant Slayer
items.description: Passive: for felling something ten levels above you.

tools.title: System registry
tools.hint: Each progression system’s working rules live in the Systems designer: its attributes and resources, what a level costs and brings, classes and skills with their requirements, and every character’s sheet. Nothing is awarded on its own: you log experience and place points.

tools.title: Classes & Jobs
tools.hint: Whether a class and a Job are the same thing is yours to decide: “Kind” is only a label you can rename or empty.

tools.title: Skills & abilities
tools.hint: Notes on a skill as the story knows it. A skill with working rules (costs worked out, requirements checked) is defined once, in Systems.

tools.title: Skill evolution
tools.hint: Which skill grows into which, and what it takes.

tools.title: Ranks & tiers
tools.hint: Any ladder, in your words: F to SSS, realms, circles. Say what a rank measures; power, mastery, rarity and standing are not assumed to be the same.

tools.title: Rank progression
tools.hint: How each character’s level or realm climbs chapter by chapter, from their progression snapshots.

tools.title: Evolutions & transformations
tools.hint: Each change with where it happens. Write the state before and after in its notes; earlier states are never overwritten.

tools.title: Inventories & equipment
tools.hint: What each character carries at a point in the story.

tools.title: Progression history
tools.hint: Log and compare a character’s whole state at any chapter.

definition.name: Superhero & Superpower
definition.genre: Superhero fiction, powered urban fantasy, superhuman SF
definition.description: Define powers with their limits and counters, who has them and how well, secret identities, hero and villain organizations, and the battles between them.

tools.title: Power registry
tools.hint: What a power is, defined once. How well a given character commands it is kept apart, under Character powers.

tools.title: Character powers
tools.hint: Who has which power, and their command of it. Two characters can share a power and differ here.

tools.title: Limitations & weaknesses
tools.hint: To make a limit binding, establish it as a fact in Canon from the power’s Codex page; Continuity can then check the manuscript against it.

tools.title: Power interactions
tools.hint: Only what you record: powers are never combined or ruled on for you.

tools.title: Secret identities
tools.hint: Who is behind the mask, and who knows. The secret’s reveal and what each character believes belong on the character’s Secrets tab.

tools.title: Hero & villain organizations
tools.hint: The project’s factions: the same records the Codex and a character’s affiliations use.

tools.title: Power evolution
tools.hint: How a character’s powers change, and in which chapter.

tools.title: Battles & incidents
tools.hint: One record a battle, pointed at by every character who was in it.

tools.title: Systems designer
tools.hint: Give powers working rules: ranks, costs worked out by formula, requirements that are checked.

definition.name: Contemporary Fiction & Social Dynamics
definition.genre: Contemporary drama, slice of life, coming of age, family drama
definition.description: Keep the practical side of modern lives: social circles and family, work and school, routines, goals, money and the places people actually spend their days.

tools.title: Social circles
tools.hint: The project’s groups and organizations, the same records a character’s affiliations use.

tools.title: Who belongs where
tools.hint: How each character stands in each circle.

tools.title: Family structures
tools.hint: Drawn from the family relationships in Relationships. Add or change them there.

tools.title: Daily routines
tools.hint: For your reference when placing scenes. A routine never creates a scene or an event.

tools.title: Personal goals
tools.hint: A goal that carries a storyline can name its plot thread.

tools.title: Finances & resources
tools.hint: Free text, in any currency or none. No model of money is imposed.

tools.title: Life events
tools.hint: The turns in a life, with the chapter each falls in.

definition.name: Fantasy Worldbuilding
definition.genre: Epic, high, low and dark fantasy
definition.description: Design magic systems and their rules, and keep spells, creatures, species, realms, mythology, artifacts and magical materials as linked records.

tools.title: Magic systems
tools.hint: The rules of each kind of magic: how it is reached, what it costs, where it stops. Every field is optional; a setting need not have mana, schools or levels.

tools.title: Who can cast what
tools.hint: What each character can do, kept apart from what the spell is.

tools.title: Species & races
tools.hint: A character points at their species from their profile (the shared field “Species”) instead of repeating its description.

tools.title: Mythology & deities
tools.hint: Gods, pantheons, myths and faiths. A religion here need not have gods or a hierarchy.

tools.title: Artifacts & relics
tools.hint: These are the project’s items: the same records the Codex and a character’s possessions use.

tools.title: Artifact history
tools.hint: Where each artifact changes hands, chapter by chapter.

tools.title: Systems designer
tools.hint: Give a magic system working rules: attributes, costs, ranks and what each ability requires.

definition.name: Mystery, Detective & Investigation
definition.description: Plan cases, suspects, clues, evidence, motives and alibis, and keep what happened apart from what is believed and what the reader has been shown.

tools.title: Cases
tools.hint: A case’s status is yours to set; nothing here decides that a mystery is solved.

tools.title: Suspects, victims & persons of interest
tools.hint: Each points at a character; a suspect need not be guilty. Their secrets proper are kept on the character’s Secrets tab.

tools.title: Clues & evidence
tools.hint: What a clue is, what it seems to show and what it really means are three fields: an interpretation is never treated as established.

tools.title: Evidence matrix
tools.hint: What each clue says about each suspect.

tools.title: Alibis
tools.hint: An alibi is a claim. “Contradicted” records that evidence disagrees with it, not that the character lied.

tools.title: Who knows what
tools.hint: What each investigator and suspect knows of each clue. What the reader has been shown is the clue’s own “Reader has seen it”.

tools.title: Red herrings
tools.hint: False trails: where each is laid and where it is cleared up.

tools.title: Revelations
tools.hint: What the reader learns and when, in the order of the manuscript: the reveal order at a glance.

tools.title: Investigation timeline
tools.hint: What actually happened, and when, is the Story Timeline’s to keep. A claim that disagrees with it can be checked in Continuity.

definition.name: Historical Fiction
definition.genre: Historical novels, period drama, alternate history
definition.description: Organize periods and events, real and invented figures, family lines, the details of daily life, points of divergence and the research behind them.

tools.title: Historical periods
tools.hint: Dates are text, so “c. 1340” or “late in the reign” are as welcome as a day.

tools.title: Events
tools.hint: “Basis” keeps what you take from the record apart from what you invent. To place an event in the story’s chronology, link it from its Timeline event.

tools.title: Historical figures
tools.hint: The project’s characters, by their relation to the historical record.

tools.title: Family lineages
tools.hint: Drawn from the family relationships in Relationships: parents and children, siblings, spouses. Add or change them there.

tools.title: Alternate history changes
tools.hint: What you change and what follows from it, as you record it; consequences are never worked out for you. A divergence can also be written as a branch of the story.

tools.title: Historical references
tools.hint: “Verification” is your own note of what you have checked. Nothing here vouches for a source.

tools.title: Chronology
tools.hint: The story’s chronology is the Timeline.

tools.title: Alternate timelines
tools.hint: Write a divergence as its own branch of the story.

definition.name: Romance & Relationship Development
definition.genre: Romance, and stories with a romantic subplot
definition.description: Plan romantic arcs: the stages a relationship moves through, its milestones and conflicts, and why the two belong together or do not.

tools.title: Romantic arcs
tools.hint: An arc points at its characters; the relationship itself (what they are to each other, chapter by chapter) stays in Relationships.

tools.title: Arcs by stage
tools.hint: The stages are a choice list you can rename, reorder, add to or cut under Categories & fields.

tools.title: Relationship stages
tools.hint: When an arc enters a stage, and the chapter that marks it. Set your own stages under Configure.

tools.title: Emotional milestones
tools.hint: Only suggestions: a story may skip or reorder any of them.

tools.title: Romantic conflicts
tools.hint: What comes between them: its cause and consequences in the notes, where it starts and where it ends.

tools.title: Emotional intensity
tools.hint: How strongly it runs at each turn, as you judge it. The points are drawn as a line through the story.

tools.title: Attraction & tension
tools.hint: Optional numbers for planning. They measure nothing but your intent.

tools.title: Relationship history
tools.hint: The full history of what two characters are to each other lives in Relationships.

definition.name: Horror & Suspense
definition.genre: Supernatural, psychological, cosmic, survival and gothic horror
definition.description: Organize threats and the rules they follow, the rise of fear across the book, incidents and their cost, and what the survivors have left.

tools.title: Threats & entities
tools.hint: A threat need not be a creature. Only the rules you write here exist; none is assumed.

tools.title: Threat rules
tools.hint: To make a rule binding, establish it as a fact in Canon from the threat’s Codex page.

tools.title: Fear & tension
tools.hint: The intensity you intend for a chapter or scene, drawn as a line through the book. It is never read off the text.

tools.title: Escalation
tools.hint: How close each danger is at each turn.

tools.title: Incidents
tools.hint: What happens, where in the book, and to whom. Its consequences go in the notes.

tools.title: What becomes of them
tools.hint: What becomes of each person, and in which chapter.

tools.title: Survival resources
tools.hint: The project’s items, sorted by what they are good for. Leave “Resource” empty on anything that is not a supply.

tools.title: Escalation timeline
tools.hint: The order things actually happen in is the Story Timeline’s to keep.
